127 years ago today — February 22, 1899 — U.S. forces under Maj. Gen. Elwell S. Otis repelled a major Filipino counterattack in the Second Battle of Manila during the Philippine-American War. 

Amid ongoing clashes after the Spanish cession, (Spanish-American War), 19,000 well-equipped American troops defended the city against ~30,000 poorly-armed insurgents from warring factions, securing key positions with artillery and disciplined fire.

This engagement solidified U.S. control over the archipelago, viewed at the time as vital to counter Japan's Pacific expansions and protect trade routes. A determined step in America's emergence as a global power.
